abstract: This lecture by Drs. Jones and Shannon provides a practical guide for primary care clinicians on assessing and treating substance use disorders. It covers the DSM-5 diagnostic criteria, severity classification, and recommended screening (USPSTF). Treatment options include various levels of care (inpatient, residential, outpatient), monitoring programs, and 12-step programs, with a focus on Celebrate Recovery as a Christ-centered alternative. The speakers also simulate a Celebrate Recovery meeting to illustrate its structure and principles.
key_points: Start assessment with the least controversial substances (caffeine, nicotine, alcohol) before moving to controlled substances.
USPSTF recommends screening all adults 18 and older for unhealthy drug use.
DSM-5 diagnosis of substance use disorder requires 2 or more of 11 criteria in a 12-month period; severity: mild (2-3), moderate (4-5), severe (6+).
Treatment includes inpatient, residential, outpatient (IOP), detox, and monitoring programs.
Monitoring programs significantly increase the likelihood of abstinence.
Recommend attendance in a 12-step program for anyone with substance use disorder; common practice is 90 meetings in 90 days.
The 12 steps are based on Christian principles but use inclusive language; each step has a corresponding principle (e.g., honesty, hope, faith).
Celebrate Recovery is Christ-centered, emphasizing that identity is in Christ, not in the problem, and includes step studies lasting 9-18 months.
Celebrate Recovery is for anyone struggling with hurts, hang-ups, and habits of any kind.
A typical Celebrate Recovery meeting includes prayer, worship, announcements, step reading, and sharing.
Step one of 12-step programs involves admitting powerlessness and unmanageability.
Refusing to admit powerlessness can lead to losing everything important.
